result.message: Reviewed the round-2 candidate (sha256 96b0e8e4…, identical in optimize_definition_output.json, .ledger.json and .best_kernel.py) against the supplied definition, oracle, correctness/timing workloads, evaluation contract, and prior preflight/evaluate/review artifacts. The candidate is a genuine Triton implementation of moe_sum_reduce (input.float().sum(dim=1).mul(routed_scaling_factor).to(input.dtype)): it contains no torch.ops / torch fallback, no reference import or dispatcher registration, no cached or shape-keyed constant outputs, no host synchronization and no environment mutation, so I found no P0 code or test-contract defect. Its two-path dispatch is arithmetically sound: the mask-free contiguous path is only taken when block_m (power of two ≤16) divides T and block_n (power of two ≤1024) divides H and input.is_contiguous(), so grid (T/block_m, H/block_n) and the flat offsets m*(K*H)+n+k*H are all in bounds; every other case (non-contiguous, odd H/T) falls to the masked strided kernel with real runtime strides. fp32 accumulation then one fp32 multiply then store cast to the input dtype reproduces the reference's fp32-sum/cast-back order, consistent with the reported abs_err 0, and the returned tensor is freshly allocated (matches effects.mutates=[] and returns_alias_of={}). The catalog oracle (oracle.py) does not import or call the candidate, and its bf16 tolerance (atol=rtol=1.5e-2) matches the workload tolerance (0.015, matched_ratio 1.0); the review_tests evaluate.json reference_source='primary' with all speedups ≈1.0 is a reference-as-solution sanity check, not proof of correctness. The findings below are advisory: (1) the authoritative final_verification retest measures three of five timing workloads below the reference (0.879/0.920/0.892) while the run summary claims every shape was lifted to 0.925/0.990/1.009 and the ledger keeps a different best_geo_mean; (2) no explicit correctness case exercises block_m>1, so the BM=16/BN=1024 path used by all five timing shapes has no supplied numerical validation; (3) the supplied test-review artifact is an explicit skip bound to a different subject sha and therefore does not evidence acceptance of this candidate's test contract.
